http_semantics.note: No client-error-shaped request; all requests well-formed per doc (op form {"delete":{"points":[12]}} matches the doc's own batch example) and all returned HTTP 200 with per-op results; the mismatch is between the oracle constant 2 and the observed 3.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: batch operations are applied sequentially in the order given; each operation reports its own result
contract_grounding.note: violates-declaration self-check: the observed end-state IS the constraint-compliant outcome — sequential in-order application of [upsert {20 x2}, delete 12] over pre-state {3,10,12} yields exactly the observed count 3 and visible set {3,10,20} with id 20 = {"try":2} (duplicate ids collapse to one point per the documented Idempotence semantics, so the upsert nets +1 and the delete nets -1: 3+1-1=3). The constraint is correctly cited (it governs in-batch ordering and per-op results); the observed value is genuinely compliant. The co-cited qdrant_behavioral_points_batch_001 ('batch update returns HTTP 200 with one result entry per operation; missing collection returns 404') is also satisfied: M2 returned 200 with exactly 2 per-op result entries; M1 returned 200 with exactly 4. The related state invariant qdrant_inv_count_consistency_001 ('upserting N points with wait=true then counting with exact=true returns count=N') likewise predicts 3, not 2: exactly 1 new point (id 20) was upserted and 1 deleted. The script's expected value 2 is arithmetically underivable from any cited constraint and contradicts the script's own docstring line '+1-1=0 relative net' and its own want_ids set of 3 elements.

script: state_points_batch_count_003.py registers POST /collections/{collection_name}/points/batch and sends M2 = [{"upsert":{"points":[{id:20,try:1},{id:20,try:2}]}},{"delete":{"points":[12]}}] with wait=true (request form matches doc example verbatim) — BUT the oracle constant at line 294-296 demands cnt == 2, contradicting the constraint-derived value 3, the script's own docstring '+1-1=0 relative net' (lines 19-20), its own inline comment arithmetic (line 282-283: 'upsert ... -> +1 (try:2 wins); delete 12 -> -1 => count 2' — 3+1-1=3, not 2), and its own want_ids {3,10,20} (3 elements, line 300) — BROKEN LINK

log: DEFECT line faithfully reports the script's oracle comparison ('exact count 3 != 2'); the raw responses beneath it ([M2 batch 2 ops] 200 with 2 per-op entries, [M2 count] count=3, [M2 get 4 ids] {3,10,20} with try:2) show an API state fully consistent with in-order sequential application — the verdict pattern is fully explained by the script-link oracle error, not by any API misbehavior
chain_trace.break_detail: The script's expected-count oracle for phase M2 is arithmetically wrong: from pre-state {3,10,12} (count 3), upserting one NEW id twice within a single op's points list (duplicate ids documented to collapse via overwrite semantics) nets +1 and deleting id 12 nets -1, so the constraint-correct count is 3 — which is exactly what the API returned, together with the exactly-correct visible set {3,10,20} and last-write-wins payload {"try":2} (both of the script's OTHER M2 checks passed against correct oracles). The script's own docstring line '+1-1=0 relative net' agrees with 3; only the coded constant (cnt != 2) and one inline comment say 2. The DEFECT_FOUND verdict is therefore an artifact of the oracle constant, not evidence of a Type4 state-logic violation in the target.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /collections/{collection_name}/points/batch -> src/actix/api/update_api.rs update_batch (line 327) -> src/common/update.rs do_batch_update_points (line 752): strict-mode pre-check pass, then a sequential 'for operation in operations' loop (line 783) dispatching each op in request order to do_upsert_points/do_delete_points/... and pushing one UpdateResult per op (line 891) -> upsert reaches lib/shard/src/update.rs upsert_points (line 181), where the points list is folded into an AHashMap<PointIdType, _> keyed by id (line 190): duplicate ids within ONE upsert op collapse to a single map entry with the LAST entry's payload (HashMap insert-overwrite), then each id is updated-or-inserted once (lines 195-252) -> delete removes ids -> readback: count (lib/collection/src/collection/point_ops.rs:407) sums stored points across shards; retrieve (line 443) dedups by id via covered_point_ids HashMap (lines 500-514). No re-validation layer reverses any of this. Source semantics therefore dictate: M2 [upsert {20 try:1},{20 try:2}; delete 12] over {3,10,12} => exactly one new point id 20 carrying {"try":2}, id 12 gone => final count 3, visible {3,10,20} — precisely what the log observed.
